question.instructions: Do the supplied dependency declarations separate runtime dependencies from development tooling?

suggest.false: Move test, lint and build tools into a development dependency group so production installs stay minimal.
suggest.abstain: Point SWAG at the dependency files (pyproject.toml or requirements files) so it can check them.

requirements.title: Choose a test organization for this project

question.instructions: Which organization is appropriate for the supplied tests and project constraints?

criteria.separate_directories: Separate unit, integration and boundary tests into explicit directories.
criteria.explicit_groups: Keep tests together with explicit groups and independently selectable commands.

suggest.separate_directories: Split tests into unit, integration and boundary directories and give each its own command.
suggest.explicit_groups: Keep one test tree and mark groups so each can run on its own.
suggest.abstain: Share the test layout and how tests are run so SWAG can recommend an organization.

question.instructions: How many of these check categories does the supplied CI configuration explicitly invoke: linting, formatting, type checking and tests? Count a category only when an identifiable command runs it. This is configuration coverage only; it does not verify execution or required branch checks.
criteria: None of the four categories is invoked.

suggest.0: Add a CI job that runs the tests, then add linting, formatting and type checking.
suggest.1: Add the missing check categories to CI; tests and a linter come first.
suggest.2: Add the remaining check categories so CI covers linting, formatting, type checking and tests.
suggest.3: Add the one missing check category to CI.
suggest.abstain: Share the CI configuration files so SWAG can count the checks they run.
